messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: router.request.latency.p99 spike detected across usw2 and euw1 at 11:04 UTC. p95 jumped from ~320ms to ~1.1s, p99 to ~3.1s. Paging on-call.
sara_oncall: I'm on pager. pulling context now.
anya_prod: I'm seeing a bunch of streaming stalls and client-side timeouts. A few customers report partial streaming responses with stuck tokens.
miguel_infra: checking LB state and router pools. Any recent routing policy rollout?
sara_oncall: yes, we deployed router-config v3.2.0 at 10:50 UTC to adjust weights for region balancing.
zoe_sre: dashboards: https://dash.redwood/internal/router/latency -> clear spike correlated to a handful of shards.
anya_prod: quick log tail from an affected proxy:
```
2026-03-14T11:05:22Z router[shard=99] WARN kv-cache miss, blocking on remote fetch
2026-03-14T11:05:23Z router[shard=99] ERROR request backpressure applied
```
anya_prod: also seeing clients hashed to shard 13 suddenly landing on shard 99 on ~30% of proxies.
ryan_platform: that sounds like inconsistent hash seeds across proxies. Could the rollout have changed consistent_hash_seed without atomic apply?
miguel_infra: running `routerctl metrics query 'router_shard_load' --region=usw2` -> shard 99 at 0.71 load share, others ~0.02-0.05.
sara_oncall: immediate mitigations? rollback, push-config, or emergency weight adjust?
zoe_sre: short test: reduce weight on shard 99 in usw2 to 0.15 and force config sync to proxies. If we don't see improvement in 10-12m, rollback.
miguel_infra: applying emergency weight change:
`routerctl set-weight --shard 99 --region usw2 --weight 0.15 --reason "emergency hotshard reduction"`
miguel_infra: pushing config to all proxies: `routerctl push-config --sync --timeout 60s`
anya_prod: within 90s queue depth for shard 99 dropped by about 55%. p99 started to decline.
sara_oncall: p99 now ~1.05s, p95 ~360ms. Streaming stalls decreased. Good.
customer-success-bot: CS update: Customer Polaris reported restored streaming; ticket #CS-4821 updated.
ryan_platform: need root cause: pulled configs from canary and prod proxies. Found inconsistent field:
```
canary: consistent_hash_seed: 987654321
prod:   consistent_hash_seed: 123456789
```
ryan_platform: seed drift explains why same keys hashed to different shards on different proxies.
miguel_infra: v3.2.0 changed weight calc and updated seed. Rollout tooling didn't verify seed uniformity before marking success.
zoe_sre: actions: 1) run controlled rollback to v3.1.4 to restore stable seeds 2) add pre-rollout seed-consistency check 3) add canary gate that verifies hash outputs across proxies before scaling rollout
sara_oncall: authorizing rollback. miguel please proceed and keep me updated.
miguel_infra: rollback started: `routerctl rollback --version v3.1.4 --target usw2,euw1 --force` -> 92% proxies reverted, remainder catching up
sara_oncall: monitoring metrics. p99 steady ~380ms, p95 ~330ms. No new increases.
anya_prod: exported traces and logs to s3: s3://incidents/router-hotkey/2076543210/ for post-incident analysis.
ryan_platform: I'll own postmortem and add a control-plane validation check to reject rollouts with non-uniform consistent_hash_seed. Also propose adding a canary test that sends sampled keys and verifies consistent routing across canaries.
zoe_sre: schedule follow-up in 90 minutes. Add action owners: ryan_platform (postmortem + control-plane fixes), miguel_infra (rollout tooling), anya_prod (trace analysis), sara_oncall (incident reviewer).
sara_oncall: incident state -> MITIGATED, switching to monitoring. I'll hold pager for 30 more minutes then rotate.
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-031 created and status set to MITIGATED by sara_oncall. Postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
